image.subject: Aslan, a huge golden-tawny lion with a shining mane, calm and majestic, standing in light on bare new earth at the edge of a young wood, lifting his head as the soil around him stirs

storyboard.claim: Aslan's power joins with the world instead of forcing it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the lion stands calm in light while the ground stirs around him
storyboard.relationToPrevious: opens the contrast between the two kinds of power
storyboard.addedInformation: calm participatory power, not domination

image.subject: a tall woman with long black hair in a dark gown and silver crown, standing in a stone hall, calm and regal

storyboard.claim: Jadis recognises a magic older than her own.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jadis at the wood's edge, face shadowed with fear, looking at the lion
storyboard.addedInformation: her fear shows the power is older than hers

image.subject: Jadis in her long dark gown gripping a heavy black iron bar in both hands, stepping forward into a clearing, her face fearful

storyboard.claim: Jadis arms herself with an iron bar brought from London.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jadis in a clearing with the iron bar raised
storyboard.relationToPrevious: her fear turns into an attack
storyboard.addedInformation: the bar is a London object, the mechanical weapon of the story

image.subject: a heavy iron bar flying through the air toward a golden lion's head, the lion calm and unflinching, walking on with his head level

storyboard.claim: Jadis throws the bar at the lion, and he does not react.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the iron bar in mid-air aimed at the lion's head
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the attack from the previous beat
storyboard.addedInformation: the lion is unharmed

image.subject: Aslan walking on through a clearing, the iron bar lying half-buried in dark fresh soil at his feet

storyboard.claim: The bar falls into the new soil and does nothing to the lion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the iron bar sinking into dark earth while the lion walks past
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the bar lands after the failed strike
storyboard.addedInformation: the new soil is the first sign of the world's power

image.subject: close view of the iron bar lying in fresh dark soil, pale green shoots pushing up beside it

storyboard.claim: The new soil is full of growth, and it begins to act on the metal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: green shoots rising beside the iron bar in dark soil
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the bar in the soil from the previous beat
storyboard.addedInformation: growth has started on the dead metal

image.subject: a black iron bar rising from the soil as a lamp-post, its metal branching out and its lamp flickering with yellow flame, in a bright new forest

storyboard.claim: The iron bar grows into a living lamp-post.
storyboard.concreteVisual: an iron lamp-post growing branches and flickering with flame
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the shoots from the previous beat turn the bar into a plant
storyboard.addedInformation: the lamp-post is the London street object that becomes a living thing

image.subject: Jadis at the edge of the wood, her face half in shadow, looking at the sprouting lamp-post

storyboard.claim: Jadis's power has a limit: here everything is absorbed into growth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jadis staring at the lamp-post that is growing
storyboard.addedInformation: her destructive intent meets a world that creates

image.subject: the lamp-post's iron branches softly sprouting green leaves, its flame steady, in a sunlit new wood

storyboard.claim: A weapon of destruction becomes something that grows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: iron branches now in leaf around a lamp-post
storyboard.addedInformation: the end of the destructive object

image.subject: Jadis running in her long dark gown through a dim new wood between pale trunks, her silver crown glinting, fleeing

storyboard.claim: Jadis cannot undo the making, so she runs into the woods.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jadis fleeing through the trees
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the lamp-post shows she cannot stop creation
storyboard.addedInformation: she is driven out by creation

image.subject: mounds of dark earth heaving open in a sunlit clearing, a deer and a panther shaking soil from their coats

storyboard.claim: Animals burst out of the earth in a solemn, majestic moment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a deer and a panther shaking earth from their coats in a clearing
storyboard.addedInformation: the animals are born from the earth

storyboard.claim: The grand creation scene is about to be undercut by a joke.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a plain dark card with one word set large, the stillness of creation held before the turn
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the awe of the creation scene
storyboard.addedInformation: sets up the comic turn

storyboard.claim: Aslan gives the animals consciousness, and the joke lands.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a clearing of animals, one after another lifting their heads to look at each other for the first time
storyboard.addedInformation: the punchline announces the gift

image.subject: Aslan lowering his great golden head over a pair of deer, warm breath visibly misting in the cold air of a new clearing

storyboard.claim: Aslan breathes life into the animals.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aslan's breath misting over a pair of deer
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the gift of consciousness from the joke
storyboard.addedInformation: the breath is the act of giving speech

image.subject: a chestnut London cab horse still wearing worn leather harness, turning its head in a bright new forest, mouth open as if speaking

storyboard.claim: The cab horse Strawberry speaks first and undercuts the tension.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Strawberry turning to speak in a new forest
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the breath gave the animals speech
storyboard.addedInformation: the first words are humble, not grand

image.subject: a black jackdaw perched on a low branch, wings half open, beak open mid-shout, while a line of animals stares up at it in silence

storyboard.claim: A jackdaw shouts a poorly timed comment in a silent crowd.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a jackdaw on a branch with beak open above silent animals
storyboard.addedInformation: a comic break in the silence

image.subject: a rabbit and a fox with their faces screwed up, stifling laughter, in a sunlit clearing

storyboard.claim: The animals struggle not to laugh at the jackdaw.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a rabbit and a fox stifling laughter
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the jackdaw's shout in the silence
storyboard.addedInformation: the humour is shared by the animals

storyboard.claim: Why undercut the majesty of creation with humour?
storyboard.concreteVisual: a plain dark card, the jackdaw's shout still hanging over a silent clearing
storyboard.addedInformation: humour is proof of free will

left.label: CHARN
left.subject: the silent, red-lit ruined city of Charn, empty towers and a great bell in a dead square, no living thing in sight

right.label: NARNIA
right.subject: a bright new Narnian clearing with animals gathered and laughing together under a new sky

storyboard.claim: A solemn, fearful creation would be a dictatorship like Charn.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Charn's silent square beside a laughing Narnian clearing
storyboard.addedInformation: the difference between Jadis's world and Aslan's

storyboard.claim: Aslan tells the animals to laugh and fear not, so the universe is built on joy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a plain card with Aslan's command set large, the animals in the background of a bright clearing
storyboard.addedInformation: Aslan's explicit permission to laugh

storyboard.claim: Laughter needs perspective, surprise and no fear.
storyboard.concreteVisual: three short lines on a bright card, with the animals laughing in the background
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the joy of the previous beat
storyboard.addedInformation: the three conditions for laughter

design.kicker: THE APPLE AND THE GARDEN'S GATE

storyboard.claim: The emotional climax begins, and Digory's grief is still there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a chapter title card on a dark ground, the turn to the climax held in the silence
storyboard.onScreenText: THE APPLE AND THE GARDEN'S GATE
storyboard.addedInformation: chapter card for the climax

image.subject: Mrs Kirke: a pale thin Edwardian woman in a white nightgown and shawl, lying in a narrow bed in a dim upstairs room, frail and weary

storyboard.claim: Digory's mother is still dying in London.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mrs Kirke in bed in a dim room
storyboard.addedInformation: the reason for Digory's grief and his burden

image.subject: Digory, a slim English boy of about eleven, short untidy brown hair, grey wool jacket and short trousers, scuffed boots, shifting his weight and turning his face away from a huge golden-tawny lion

storyboard.claim: Digory faces the lion and tries to avoid blame.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory turning his face away from the lion
storyboard.addedInformation: his instinct to deflect

image.subject: Uncle Andrew: an old man, wild grey hair, a sharply pointed nose, a dressing gown over a waistcoat, pale vain face, holding up a yellow ring in a dusty attic study

storyboard.claim: Digory blames his uncle for sending the children away by magic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Uncle Andrew holding up a yellow ring in the attic
storyboard.addedInformation: the uncle who sent them into other worlds

storyboard.claim: Aslan asks whether Digory met the witch, and he cannot hide.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a plain card with the question, the lion's great face bending close in the background
storyboard.addedInformation: the lion sees through the excuse

image.subject: Digory standing beside a great bell in the red-lit ruined city of Charn, his head bowed, a grey wool jacket on a small slim boy

storyboard.claim: Digory admits he struck the bell that woke Jadis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory bowed beside the great bell of Charn
storyboard.addedInformation: the bell is the origin of the disaster

image.subject: Digory kneeling on dusty ground in a sunlit clearing, head bowed, hands open at his sides, shaking

storyboard.claim: Digory chose his pride and is now completely exposed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory kneeling, head bowed, in a clearing
storyboard.addedInformation: his grief starts to overwhelm his fear

storyboard.claim: Digory begs for a cure, but he has nothing to bargain with.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory's empty hands open on the grass, the lion's shadow falling over him
storyboard.addedInformation: he cannot bargain with a god

image.subject: Digory looking up at the stern, unyielding face of a huge golden-tawny lion, lit from above, expecting judgment

storyboard.claim: Digory expects a stern judgment from the lion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory looking up at the lion's stern face
storyboard.addedInformation: the expected face of judgment

image.subject: close view of a huge golden lion's face, his eyes glistening with great shining tears standing in his fur

storyboard.claim: The lion's eyes hold tears, not judgment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a close view of the lion's eyes with shining tears
storyboard.addedInformation: the lion weeps

storyboard.claim: Aslan says: my son, my son, I know.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a plain quotation card with Aslan's words set large, the lion's voice implied by the empty ground
storyboard.onScreenText: MY SON, MY SON, I KNOW
storyboard.addedInformation: a direct quotation of the lion's words

image.subject: Digory, a grey-jacketed boy with short untidy brown hair, resting his hand on a golden lion's mane, both standing in soft light

storyboard.claim: Aslan and Digory share the grief, and only they know it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Digory's hand on the lion's mane in soft light
storyboard.addedInformation: the tender bond between the boy and the lion

left.label: JADIS
left.subject: Jadis, cold and untouched, standing apart in a red-lit ruined hall

right.label: ASLAN
right.subject: Aslan, a huge golden lion with tears in his eyes, leaning close to a small boy in soft light

storyboard.claim: Mythic gods stand untouched by suffering; Aslan is touched by it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jadis apart in a ruined hall beside Aslan leaning close to the boy
storyboard.addedInformation: the contrast of the removed god and the compassionate one

image.subject: Aslan, a huge golden-tawny lion, standing on a hill under a sky full of new stars, the first forest spreading below, a single tear on his cheek

storyboard.claim: Aslan is creating a whole cosmos and still weeps for one boy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the lion on a hill under a sky of stars with a tear
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the contrast with the removed gods
storyboard.addedInformation: the scale of the cosmos against one grief

storyboard.claim: Vulnerability separates the divine from the tyrannical.
storyboard.concreteVisual: two words set against each other on a dark ground, one soft and one hard
storyboard.addedInformation: empathy legitimises his power

storyboard.claim: Empathy is not a magical quick fix; Aslan does not cure the mother with a snap.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a plain card with a question, a bed-side silence and no cure in sight
storyboard.addedInformation: sets up the healing quest
